topology_reasoning.device_identification: A symmetric two-waveguide adiabatic directional coupler. Two isolated input guides approach one another through mirrored smooth S-bends, reach a narrow-gap interaction region near the longitudinal center, and then separate through mirrored S-bends to two isolated output ports.
topology_reasoning.operating_principle: Evanescent supermodes form while the guides are close. The minimum edge gap, local guide widths, and the longitudinal extent/profile of the close approach set accumulated coupling; the smooth approach and exit reduce transition loss and parasitic mode conversion.
observations: The material bounding box exactly fills the calibrated 18.0 um by 3.0 um footprint.
Both guides are mirror symmetric about y = 1.5 um and approximately symmetric about x = 9.0 um.
Each guide has an approximately constant normal width of 0.66 um.
The isolated-port center pitch is approximately 2.34 um; the closest center pitch is approximately 0.95 um, implying a minimum edge gap near 0.29-0.30 um.
The guide widening visible in vertical pixel slices over the slopes is consistent with constant-width normal extrusion, not a physical width taper.

function_defining_knobs.wg_width: guide core width and modal confinement
function_defining_knobs.tip_width: interaction-region guide width; initialized equal to wg_width because the reference is constant-width
function_defining_knobs.gap: minimum edge-to-edge separation and dominant coupling-strength control
function_defining_knobs.transfer_length: length of the near-parallel central interaction region
function_defining_knobs.taper_length: longitudinal width-transition span from port width to interaction tip width
function_defining_knobs.approach_length: span of each smooth separation-changing approach/exit
function_defining_knobs.port_pitch: center-to-center separation at the four isolated ports
function_defining_knobs.lead_length: horizontal lead length before and after the smooth coupling profile
function_defining_knobs.phase_trim_length: single-guide output trim used as a real path-length/phase knob; zero in the faithful recreation

topology_reasoning.geometry_plan: Construct both mirrored centerlines as sampled analytic gf.Path objects and extrude them on layer (1, 0). Use horizontal leads, a smooth raised-cosine approach, a central near-parallel transfer section, and the mirrored exit. Use path extrusion and primitive tapers only; emit no raw polygons and no pre-built device cell.

iterations.change_made: Initial primitives-only implementation: two mirrored sampled gf.Path centerlines with constant-width path extrusion, calibrated port pitch/minimum gap, smooth measured approach profile, and exact 18.0 um by 3.0 um material bbox. The residual diff is limited to thin alternating boundary traces from subpixel centerline/edge differences; the requested IoU stop threshold was exceeded, so no further comparison iteration was run.

knob_verification.reason_for_choice: The evaluator's response contract is specifically a differential path-length and layer-area check. phase_trim_length is a genuine coherent-device phase/path knob whose zero baseline preserves the symmetric reference; the coupling-specific gap, transfer length, taper lengths, and tip widths remain live top-level geometry knobs.
knob_verification.serialization_note: The first diagnostic invocation exposed that GDSFactory metadata made the context cell the only gdstk top-level cell, so the evaluator skipped all geometry. Writing the identical component with with_metadata=False made the decorated assembly the measurable top cell; the final mandated check then passed.
